liveUpdates.text: AMRO maintains ASEAN+3 2026 growth forecast at 4.0%, raises inflation projection to 1.8%.
Asian teams remain undefeated in opening matches of the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
Infrastructure Asia signs US$16 billion in MoUs at the Asia Infrastructure Forum 2026.
Magnus Carlsen claims victory at the inaugural 2026 ASEAN E-Sports Chess Cup in Bangkok.
Future of Asia Forum kicks off in Tokyo with focus on global economic integration.

articles.title: Historic Start for Asian Teams at the 2026 FIFA World Cup
articles.excerpt: AFC teams make an unprecedented undefeated start, with South Korea, Australia, and Japan securing vital points against European giants.
articles.content:
The 2026 FIFA World Cup has kicked off with a historic surge from Asian Football Confederation (AFC) teams, marking their most successful opening round in tournament history. As of mid-June, none of the Asian teams have suffered a defeat in their opening fixtures, signaling a major power shift in international football.

South Korea secured a thrilling 2-1 victory over the Czech Republic, showcasing their tactical maturity and lethal counter-attacking prowess. Meanwhile, Australia outclassed Turkey with a solid 2-0 win, relying on their robust defensive organization and set-piece efficiency.

Japan fought to a hard-earned 2-2 draw against a heavily favored Netherlands side, demonstrating remarkable resilience and technical ability. Analysts point to a tactical shift among Asian teams, which now prioritize defensive solidity and leverage the vast European-league experience of their core players.

This unprecedented start has ignited massive celebrations across the continent, raising hopes that an Asian team could reach the semi-finals or beyond for the first time since 2002.
articles.author: Kenji Matsuda

articles.title: AMRO Maintains 4.0% Growth Forecast for ASEAN+3 Amid Rising Inflation Concerns
articles.excerpt: The ASEAN+3 Macroeconomic Research Office projects steady growth but warns of persistent inflation driven by Middle East disruptions.
articles.content:
The ASEAN+3 Macroeconomic Research Office (AMRO) has released its interim June 2026 update, maintaining its robust 4.0% economic growth forecast for the ASEAN+3 region. The steady growth projection highlights the region's resilience in the face of ongoing global economic headwinds and shifting trade dynamics.

However, AMRO has upwardly revised its inflation projections for the region from 1.4% to 1.8%. The agency cited persistent supply chain disruptions and volatile energy prices, primarily stemming from the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, as the main drivers of the inflationary pressure.

"While the region's growth trajectory remains solid, policymakers must remain vigilant," stated AMRO's chief economist during the briefing in Singapore. "The imported inflation from energy and commodity markets poses a complex challenge for central banks trying to balance growth with price stability."

The report advises regional governments to prioritize targeted fiscal support and continue structural reforms to enhance long-term economic resilience. It also emphasized the importance of intra-regional trade to buffer against external shocks.
articles.author: Lim Wei Chen

articles.title: Asia Infrastructure Forum 2026 Secures US$16 Billion in Sustainable Financing Pacts
articles.excerpt: Infrastructure Asia signs four major MoUs to boost project bankability and green infrastructure across South and Southeast Asia.
articles.content:
The Asia Infrastructure Forum (AIF) 2026 concluded with a massive leap for regional development, as Infrastructure Asia announced the signing of four major Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) totaling over US$16 billion in potential investments. The forum, held in Singapore, focused heavily on sustainable and green infrastructure projects.

The agreements aim to enhance project bankability and accelerate the financing of critical infrastructure across South and Southeast Asia. Key areas of focus include renewable energy grids, sustainable water management systems, and smart city developments designed to withstand the impacts of climate change.

"These MoUs represent a tangible commitment from both public and private sectors to bridge the infrastructure gap in Asia sustainably," said the Executive Director of Infrastructure Asia. "We are moving beyond dialogue to deploy real capital into projects that will drive inclusive economic growth."

The financing will be channeled through a mix of multilateral development banks, sovereign wealth funds, and private institutional investors, marking a new era of blended finance in the region.
articles.author: Priya Sharma

articles.title: Magnus Carlsen Triumphs at Inaugural ASEAN E-Sports Chess Cup in Bangkok
articles.excerpt: The chess grandmaster secured the title in Thailand, highlighting the rapid convergence of traditional chess and the booming Asian e-sports market.
articles.content:
World Chess Champion Magnus Carlsen has added another accolade to his legendary career, winning the inaugural 2026 ASEAN E-Sports Chess Cup held in Bangkok, Thailand. The tournament, which concluded on June 13, represents a significant milestone in integrating classical chess with the massive Asian e-sports ecosystem.

Carlsen faced fierce competition from a new generation of Asian grandmasters and e-sports prodigies, ultimately securing the title in a tense rapid-play tiebreaker against India's rising star. The event drew massive online viewership, breaking streaming records for chess in the Southeast Asian region.

The tournament's success underscores the booming popularity of e-sports in Asia. Organizers highlighted that blending chess with high-production e-sports broadcasting has attracted a younger, highly engaged demographic.

"The atmosphere in Bangkok was electric, rivaling any major traditional sporting event," Carlsen commented after his victory. "The passion for competitive gaming and chess in this region is truly remarkable." Local authorities plan to make the Cup an annual fixture on the Asian e-sports calendar.
articles.author: Niran Somchai

articles.title: Asia-Pacific Pro AV Market Skyrockets to US$123.7 Billion Driven by AI Integration
articles.excerpt: The professional audiovisual market in APAC experiences explosive growth, fueled by investments in smart workplaces and digital infrastructure.
articles.content:
The Asia-Pacific professional audiovisual (Pro AV) market has reached a staggering valuation of US$123.7 billion in 2026, according to the newly released 'Asia-Pacific Pro AV Market Playbook.' The report highlights the region as the global engine for AV technology adoption and innovation.

The unprecedented growth is largely driven by massive corporate investments in artificial intelligence, smart workplaces, and advanced digital infrastructure across tech hubs like Singapore, Seoul, and Shenzhen. Companies are rapidly upgrading their facilities to support hybrid work models and immersive collaboration tools.

"We are seeing a paradigm shift where AV is no longer just about screens and speakers, but integrated AI-driven environments that enhance productivity and user experience," noted industry analyst Sarah Jenkins. The integration of AI for automated language translation, smart camera framing, and predictive maintenance has become the new standard.

The education and healthcare sectors are also major contributors to this growth, deploying advanced AV systems for remote learning and telemedicine. The booming market presents lucrative opportunities for tech manufacturers and integrators operating within the APAC region.
articles.author: David Chen

articles.title: Future of Asia Forum Convenes in Tokyo to Address Global Market Volatility
articles.excerpt: Political and economic leaders gather at the Nikkei event to discuss policy coordination and Asia's evolving role in a fragmented global economy.
articles.content:
The annual Future of Asia Forum, hosted by Nikkei, kicked off in Tokyo this week, bringing together heads of state, central bank governors, and leading CEOs from across the region. The prestigious two-day event (June 10-11) focused on Asia's strategic response to increasing global market volatility and geopolitical fragmentation.

Keynote speakers emphasized the urgent need for enhanced regional economic integration to buffer against external shocks, particularly the ongoing fluctuations in US Federal Reserve interest rates and Middle East-driven oil price instability. Discussions centered on strengthening intra-Asian supply chains and expanding local currency settlement mechanisms.

Japanese Prime Minister addressed the forum, advocating for a 'free and open economic architecture' that prioritizes technological innovation and sustainable growth. 'Asia must transition from being the world's factory to being the world's innovation engine,' he stated.

The forum also tackled the delicate balance of navigating US-China trade tensions, with many Southeast Asian leaders reiterating their commitment to neutrality and open trade. The consensus emerging from Tokyo is that Asia must proactively shape global economic rules rather than merely reacting to them.
articles.author: Takashi Yamamoto

articles.title: Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games Unveils Comprehensive E-Sports Schedule
articles.excerpt: Organizers announce the full lineup for e-sports medal events, reflecting the discipline's formal integration into the Asian sporting calendar.
articles.content:
The organizing committee for the 20th Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, has officially unveiled the comprehensive competition schedule for all e-sports events. This marks a historic moment, solidifying e-sports as an official medal discipline following its highly successful debut at the Hangzhou Games.

The 2026 roster will feature a mix of globally popular team-based battle arenas (MOBAs), tactical shooters, and digital sports simulations. Organizers noted that the selection process prioritized games with deep roots in Asian gaming culture and massive regional player bases.

Ticket sales for the highly anticipated e-sports finals are set to begin on June 30, 2026, and are expected to sell out within hours. To accommodate the massive expected turnout, the e-sports events will be hosted in a newly retrofitted, state-of-the-art digital arena in Nagoya, equipped with ultra-low latency infrastructure.

National Olympic Committees across Asia are already finalizing their rosters, treating e-sports athletes with the same rigorous training regimens and support structures as traditional athletes. The Aichi-Nagoya Games are poised to set a new benchmark for competitive gaming on the international stage.
articles.author: Jin Woo

articles.title: NGOs Warn Against Fossil Fuel Expansion in the Coral Triangle Amid Energy Crunch
articles.excerpt: Environmental coalitions push back against new drilling proposals, highlighting severe risks to marine biodiversity and regional fisheries.
articles.content:
A powerful coalition of environmental NGOs and marine scientists has issued a stark warning regarding proposed fossil fuel expansions within the Coral Triangle. The region, which spans the waters of Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands, and Timor-Leste, is widely recognized as the global epicenter of marine biodiversity.

The controversy stems from recent governmental proposals to open new offshore tracts for oil and gas exploration to alleviate ongoing regional energy shortages and price volatility. Industry proponents argue the expansion is necessary for energy security and economic development.

However, the NGO coalition emphasizes that drilling in these fragile ecosystems poses an existential threat to the marine life that supports the livelihoods of over 120 million people. "The short-term energy gains cannot justify the irreversible destruction of the world's most critical reef systems," stated Dr. Maria Santos, lead marine biologist for the coalition.

The groups are actively lobbying for a pivot towards aggressive investments in renewable energy alternatives, specifically offshore wind and tidal energy, which they argue can meet the region's energy demands without jeopardizing the marine environment. The debate highlights the intense friction between immediate energy needs and long-term environmental sustainability in Southeast Asia.
articles.author: Anita Rizal

articles.title: Retail’s Big Show Asia Pacific Focuses on AI and Consumer Connectivity
articles.excerpt: The massive retail expo in Singapore showcases the future of shopping, dominated by predictive analytics and seamless omnichannel experiences.
articles.content:
Retail's Big Show Asia Pacific (June 2-4) concluded in Singapore, drawing thousands of industry executives, tech innovators, and brands to discuss the rapid transformation of the region's retail landscape. The consensus was clear: the future of Asian retail is hyper-connected and driven by artificial intelligence.

Exhibitors showcased next-generation retail technologies, ranging from AI-powered predictive inventory systems that anticipate local demand trends, to augmented reality (AR) fitting rooms that seamlessly blend online and offline shopping experiences. The focus has shifted from mere digitization to creating frictionless, deeply personalized consumer journeys.

"Asia-Pacific consumers are the most digitally fluent in the world. They don't just expect convenience; they demand anticipatory service," explained a keynote speaker from a leading regional e-commerce giant. The adoption of social commerce and integrated digital wallets was also highlighted as a critical growth vector.

The event underscored the intense competition in the APAC retail sector, where traditional brick-and-mortar stores are aggressively partnering with tech firms to survive the digital onslaught. Brands that fail to integrate robust data analytics and seamless connectivity risk being rapidly outpaced in this fast-moving commercial region.
articles.author: Sarah Lee

articles.title: Indian Squash Veteran Joshna Chinappa Qualifies for Historic 7th Asian Games
articles.excerpt: The legendary athlete continues to defy age, securing her spot for the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Games and inspiring a new generation of players.
articles.content:
Indian squash icon Joshna Chinappa has once again etched her name into the history books, officially qualifying for the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games. This remarkable achievement makes her the first Indian athlete across any sport to compete in seven consecutive Asian Games, a testament to her enduring skill and physical resilience.

Chinappa, now approaching the twilight of her career, secured her qualification through a series of grueling national trials, defeating competitors nearly half her age. Her aggressive playing style and unparalleled tactical experience proved too much for the younger generation to overcome.

"I never imagined I would be competing at this level for this long," Chinappa shared in an emotional press conference. "Representing India at the Asian Games has always been the highest honor. I am going to Nagoya to compete for a medal, not just to participate."

Her qualification has sparked widespread celebration in the Indian sports community, where she is revered as a pioneer for women's sports. Analysts note that her presence on the team provides invaluable mentorship to India's rising squash talents as they prepare for the intense pressure of the continental stage.
articles.author: Vikram Singh

articles.title: Chinese Universities Dominate 8th Asian University 3x3 Basketball Championship
articles.excerpt: Guangdong University of Technology and Peking University sweep the titles in Zhoushan, securing their spots for the FISU World Cup.
articles.content:
The 8th Asian University 3x3 Basketball Championship, held in the coastal city of Zhoushan, China, concluded with total dominance from the host nation's collegiate programs. Both the men's and women's titles were claimed by Chinese universities in a spectacular display of fast-paced, physical streetball.

In the men's division, the formidable squad from Guangdong University of Technology powered their way through the tournament undefeated, overpowering a resilient Mongolian team in the final. Their relentless inside scoring and stifling perimeter defense proved unanswerable.

The women's tournament saw Peking University emerge victorious, utilizing their superior shooting accuracy and tactical spacing to dismantle the defending champions from Chinese Taipei. Both winning teams have now secured automatic qualification for the highly anticipated FISU University World Cup later this year.

The massive turnout and high level of play in Zhoushan underscore the explosive growth of 3x3 basketball across Asia. The format's inclusion in the Olympics has spurred heavy investment in grassroots and collegiate programs, particularly in East Asia, raising the overall standard of competition significantly.
articles.author: Michael Chang

articles.title: Philippine Gymnastics Team Eyes Asian Games at Zunyi Championships
articles.excerpt: A mix of seasoned veterans and rising junior stars compete in China, aiming to secure crucial qualification points for the 2026 Asian Games.
articles.content:
The Philippine national gymnastics team is currently battling it out at the 13th Senior and 19th Junior Asian Artistic Gymnastics Championships in Zunyi, China. The prestigious continental meet serves as a critical qualification pathway for the upcoming Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games and the World Championships.

The Philippine delegation features a strategic blend of seasoned Olympians and promising junior talents. The men's team is heavily reliant on their internationally experienced core to secure team qualification points, performing high-difficulty routines on the floor and vault.

Meanwhile, the junior women's squad has drawn attention for their elegant execution on the balance beam and uneven bars, signaling a bright future for the national program. "This competition in Zunyi is a litmus test for our readiness," stated the head coach. "The level of gymnastics in Asia is currently the highest in the world, with China and Japan leading the way."

The national federation has invested heavily in foreign training camps over the past year, and the athletes are eager to translate that preparation into podium finishes and guaranteed tickets to Nagoya later this year.
articles.author: Maria Santos

articles.title: Asian Economic Development Conference Convenes in Hong Kong to Tackle Pressing Challenges
articles.excerpt: Policymakers and researchers gather to discuss strategies for navigating shifting trade dynamics, demographic changes, and technological disruption.
articles.content:
The highly anticipated Asian Economic Development Conference (AEDC) opened its doors in Hong Kong on June 13, bringing together leading economists, central bank officials, and policy researchers from across the region. The two-day summit aims to formulate collaborative strategies to address Asia's most pressing economic challenges.

The agenda is dominated by three core themes: navigating the shifting currents of global trade amidst rising protectionism, managing the economic impacts of rapid demographic aging in East Asia, and harnessing technological disruption for inclusive growth.

In a fiery opening address, the Financial Secretary emphasized that Asia can no longer rely solely on export-led growth models tailored for Western consumer markets. "We must pivot towards stimulating robust intra-regional consumption and building resilient, localized supply chains," he argued.

Panel discussions also heavily featured the role of digital currencies and cross-border payment innovations in reducing transaction costs for SMEs. The conference is expected to culminate in a joint policy paper outlining actionable recommendations for regional governments to sustain long-term economic vitality.
articles.author: Emily Wong

articles.title: Asia-Pacific Sustainable Business Summit Opens in Jakarta with Urgent Call to Action
articles.excerpt: Corporate leaders and policymakers explore sustainable business models to drive long-term competitiveness and inclusive regional growth.
articles.content:
Jakarta is playing host to the inaugural Asia-Pacific Sustainable Business Summit (June 22-25), a massive gathering of corporate executives, ESG investors, and government ministers dedicated to accelerating the region's transition to a green economy. The summit opened with a stark warning that climate change poses the single greatest threat to Asia's economic miracle.

The event focuses on transitioning from theoretical sustainability pledges to operational realities. Workshops and keynotes cover practical strategies for decarbonizing heavy industries, establishing ethical supply chains, and mobilizing private capital for green infrastructure projects.

"Sustainability is no longer a corporate social responsibility exercise; it is the fundamental driver of future competitiveness," stated the Indonesian Minister of Finance. The summit showcased several successful regional case studies, including green hydrogen initiatives in Australia and circular economy textile manufacturing in Vietnam.

A major highlight was the launch of a new regional green taxonomy designed to standardize environmental reporting and prevent greenwashing, making it easier for global investors to identify and fund genuinely sustainable Asian enterprises.
articles.author: Budi Santoso

articles.title: Canada-ASEAN Energy Security Dialogue Underscores Need for Regional Resilience
articles.excerpt: Strategic talks highlight cooperation in natural gas exports, nuclear technology sharing, and stabilizing volatile energy markets.
articles.content:
The strategic Canada-ASEAN Energy Security Dialogue concluded today, emphasizing the critical need for enhanced cooperation to ensure reliable energy supplies in the rapidly developing Southeast Asian region. The talks come at a time of heightened anxiety over global energy volatility and the pressing need for decarbonization.

Canadian officials utilized the platform to position Canada as a stable, long-term supplier of liquefied natural gas (LNG) to fuel ASEAN's transition away from coal. Furthermore, significant discussions were held regarding the sharing of Small Modular Reactor (SMR) nuclear technology to provide reliable, zero-emission baseload power to rapidly growing Asian metropolises.

ASEAN energy ministers stressed that while the transition to renewables is the ultimate goal, natural gas remains an indispensable bridge fuel for the next two decades to support the region's aggressive industrialization goals.

The dialogue resulted in a framework agreement to facilitate joint research in grid modernization and energy storage solutions, marking a deepening of economic and strategic ties between North America and Southeast Asia.
articles.author: Liam Davies

articles.title: World Economic Forum "Summer Davos" Returns to China with Focus on AI
articles.excerpt: The Annual Meeting of the New Champions gathers global leaders to debate the impact of artificial intelligence on sustainable economic growth.
articles.content:
The World Economic Forum's Annual Meeting of the New Champions, widely known as the "Summer Davos," has convened in Dalian, China (June 23-25). The prestigious gathering of global political, business, and academic leaders is heavily focused this year on the intersection of artificial intelligence, trade resilience, and sustainable economic growth.

As AI rapidly permeates global industries, debates at the forum center on regulatory frameworks, ethical deployment, and the technology's potential to either bridge or exacerbate the economic divide between developed and developing nations in Asia.

Chinese Premier delivered a keynote address advocating for inclusive technological cooperation and warning against the fragmentation of global supply chains. "The benefits of AI must be shared globally, not hoarded behind protectionist walls," he asserted.

Sessions also tackled the resilience of Asian economies in the face of ongoing global trade realignments. Participants are working on collaborative frameworks to ensure that the rapid digitization of the Asian economy translates into tangible improvements in labor productivity and living standards across the region.
articles.author: Wei Lin

articles.title: Explainer: How the AMRO Inflation Projection Impacts Your Portfolio
articles.excerpt: Breaking down the recent ASEAN+3 macroeconomic forecast and what rising regional inflation means for retail and institutional investors.
articles.content:
The recent upward revision of inflation projections by the ASEAN+3 Macroeconomic Research Office (AMRO) from 1.4% to 1.8% might seem like a small statistical blip, but it has significant implications for investment portfolios across the Asia-Pacific.

Firstly, persistent inflation driven by energy volatility means central banks in the region are less likely to aggressively cut interest rates in the near term. For fixed-income investors, this suggests that bond yields may remain elevated, providing better income opportunities but suppressing the capital appreciation of existing bond holdings.

In the equity markets, higher inflation generally benefits sectors with strong pricing power, such as consumer staples, healthcare, and certain segments of the technology market. Conversely, companies heavily reliant on cheap borrowing or those unable to pass increased raw material costs onto consumers may see their profit margins squeezed.

Currency markets will also feel the impact. Economies that manage to contain inflation better than their neighbors often see their currencies appreciate, affecting the returns of internationally diversified portfolios. Investors are advised to focus on high-quality companies with robust balance sheets and the ability to navigate supply chain disruptions effectively.
articles.author: Financial Desk

articles.title: Explainer: The Significance of Asia's Undefeated World Cup Start
articles.excerpt: Analyzing the tactical evolutions and structural investments that have propelled Asian football to new heights on the global stage.
articles.content:
The opening days of the 2026 FIFA World Cup have produced a stunning narrative: teams from the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) are entirely undefeated against formidable international opposition. This is not merely a streak of good luck; it is the culmination of decades of strategic investment and tactical evolution.

Historically, Asian teams struggled with the physicality and tactical discipline of European and South American squads. However, a massive exodus of Asian talent to top-tier European leagues over the past decade has fundamentally changed the equation. Players from Japan, South Korea, and Australia now train and compete weekly at the highest levels of the sport, bringing invaluable experience and tactical nuance back to their national teams.

Furthermore, domestic leagues across Asia, particularly the J-League and K-League, have drastically improved their coaching standards and youth development academies. The implementation of modern sports science, data analytics, and rigorous tactical periodization has closed the physical gap.

On the pitch, this translates to highly organized defensive structures, lethal transition play, and a newfound psychological resilience. Asian teams no longer enter matches hoping for a draw; they play with a tactical arrogance previously reserved for traditional footballing superpowers.
articles.author: Sports Analysis Unit

articles.title: Opinion: Why the "Future of Asia" Demands Digital Sovereignty
articles.excerpt: As global supply chains fracture, Asian nations must prioritize building indigenous technology infrastructure to secure their economic destiny.
articles.content:
The discussions dominating the Future of Asia Forum in Tokyo this week rightly focused on economic integration and resilience. However, a crucial underlying theme requires more urgent attention: the pressing need for digital sovereignty across the Asia-Pacific.

For too long, the region has relied on Western-developed software, cloud infrastructure, and AI foundational models, while simultaneously depending on Chinese hardware manufacturing. As geopolitical tensions increasingly weaponize technology supply chains, this dual dependency poses an unacceptable strategic risk to Asia's continued economic ascent.

Asian nations must aggressively invest in indigenous technological capabilities. This doesn't mean isolationism; rather, it means developing robust, locally controlled digital infrastructure—from sovereign cloud networks to regional AI models trained on diverse Asian linguistic and cultural datasets.

By fostering a collaborative, intra-Asian technology ecosystem, the region can ensure that the next wave of digital innovation serves local needs and respects regional data privacy norms. True economic resilience in the 21st century is impossible without controlling the digital foundation upon which the modern economy is built.
articles.author: Dr. Akira Sato

articles.title: Opinion: The Coral Triangle Drilling Debate Exposes Our Broken Energy Transition
articles.excerpt: The push to explore for oil in the world's most biodiverse marine region highlights the massive funding gap for renewable energy in developing Asia.
articles.content:
The fierce controversy over new fossil fuel exploration proposals in the Coral Triangle is a tragic symptom of a much larger systemic failure. While the environmental NGOs are absolutely correct to defend this irreplaceable marine ecosystem, simply telling energy-starved developing nations "no" without providing viable alternatives is a recipe for failure.

The reality is that several Southeast Asian nations face acute energy crunches that threaten their economic stability. The transition to renewable energy is incredibly capital-intensive. While global summits celebrate pledges, the actual deployment of green finance to developing Asian nations remains sluggish, bogged down by risk aversion and bureaucratic hurdles.

If the developed world genuinely wishes to protect global biodiversity hotspots like the Coral Triangle, it must urgently de-risk and subsidize massive renewable energy projects—such as offshore wind and geothermal—in the region. The burden of environmental preservation cannot fall solely on nations struggling to keep the lights on.

Until green energy becomes the path of least resistance economically, desperate governments will continue to look toward their fossil fuel reserves, regardless of the environmental cost. The solution is not just better conservation; it is better, faster climate finance.
articles.author: Elena Rodriguez
